field_probes.label: server_ideal_activity
field_probes.role: Requested activity stored by CBaseCombatCharacter::SetIdealActivity before translation and sequence selection.

field_probes.role: Player water level tested by the compact action classifier and ordinary selector.

field_probes.label: player_action_latch
field_probes.role: One-byte latch whose retained action code is read from the adjacent 0x1cb4 dword by the classifier.

field_probes.label: player_jump_landing_state

field_probes.label: grapple_mode
field_probes.role: Nine-entry paired-action mode selecting the initial base activity and player continuation leaf.

findings.fact: vampire.dll makes 4,460 activity registrations at 0x104126e0, occupying numeric IDs 1 through 0x118c with 32 holes.
findings.evidence: The full registration body calls the activity helpers 4,460 times, from ACT_IDLE=1 through ACT_WALKIE_TALKIE=0x118c. Every registered ID is unique; StudioSeqDesc.activity is -1 on disk while szactivitynameindex is populated.
findings.consequence: The stable extraction key is the ACT_* literal; numeric IDs are pinned-build diagnostics and must not be authored into remake gameplay code.

findings.fact: CBasePlayer::PostThink calls a compact action classifier and forwards every non-negative result through the SetAnimation virtual.
findings.evidence: 0x1016be10 calls 0x1016bb50, tests against -1, and invokes vtable +0x704 with the result and zero.
findings.consequence: Player input is not a clip selector; realized player state is classified before animation mode and activity selection.

findings.fact: The player classifier returns a compact 17-entry PLAYER_* enum rather than activity IDs, and its complete symbolic vocabulary is compiled at 0x106ac3a0.
findings.evidence: 0x10429200 resolves strings against 17 pointers from PLAYER_IDLE through PLAYER_LEAVE_AIMING, while 0x1016bb50 returns movement/water/interaction/form/block values and 0x10164870 interprets them before choosing an ACT_* activity. player_action_survey.py validates every table entry against the pinned hash.
findings.consequence: Compact action and activity remain distinct enums, but the compact side is now named completely rather than awaiting trace-assigned aliases.

findings.fact: The ordinary player animation selector writes move_yaw, aim_yaw and aim_pitch, then maps every reachable compact code to a closed base or layer policy.
findings.evidence: 0x10164870 maps PLAYER_IDLE/WALK to stance and gait, PLAYER_JUMP to the phase switch, PLAYER_ATTACK1 to melee/ranged policy, PLAYER_PRAY to ACT_PRAYING_*, PLAYER_GRAPPLE to released feeding/seduction, PLAYER_SWIM, PLAYER_USE, PLAYER_LADDER, PLAYER_VOMIT, PLAYER_BLOCK and PLAYER_RELOAD to their exact branches before 0x101644f0. Codes 3, 6, 15 and 16 have no distinct branch or producer.
findings.consequence: Pose parameters and discrete activity selection are sibling outputs of one policy frame; one-shot completion and restart are handled later by the common frame-advance/apply path.

findings.fact: The complete pinned +0x704 call surface contains 15 player-animation calls and 14 unrelated NPC task-name calls at the same numeric vtable offset.
findings.evidence: player_action_survey.py scans every FF /2 call [reg+0x704] in .text. The genuine set is PostThink, paired-router re-entry, death, forced idle/walk/jump, two vomit calls, four attack paths, two reload paths and discipline Player_Anim execution; every other site is a CAI_BaseNPC task-name formatter and is dispositioned separately.
findings.consequence: PLAYER_SUPERJUMP, legacy PLAYER_FEED, PLAYER_START_AIMING and PLAYER_LEAVE_AIMING have no hidden native producer; their dormant status is a complete call-surface result.

findings.fact: Targeted-discipline Player_Anim uses the same compact enum and contributes only PLAYER_VOMIT in the effective corpus.
findings.evidence: 0x101ddfb0 reads Player_Anim, resolves it through 0x10429200 and stores the code at HitInfo+0x38; 0x101de660 passes that code to player +0x704. The patch-first vdata survey finds exactly two fields, both PLAYER_VOMIT in vdata/system/disciplinetgt_004.txt.
findings.consequence: Discipline data does not restore reachability for dormant compact codes, and its action request joins the same router as native player/weapon producers.

findings.fact: CBasePlayer and CHL2_Player share one protected-owner, ordinary-selector and SetAnimation-router implementation.
findings.evidence: The complete CBasePlayer RTTI descendant pass finds two classes; both resolve vtable +0x670 to 0x10161200, +0x684 to 0x10164870 and +0x704 to 0x10164240.
findings.consequence: Form behavior is state inside the recovered selector/router and not an undiscovered player subclass translation or commit order.

findings.fact: The ordinary player apply order is SetIdealActivity, Weapon_TranslateActivity, CBasePlayer::NPC_TranslateActivity, SetActivity, then weighted or heaviest sequence selection.
findings.evidence: 0x101644f0 returns from SetIdealActivity at 0x10164577, calls virtual +0x5f4 and returns at 0x10164582, calls virtual +0x5e0 at 0x10164587, then calls SetActivity at +0x4d8 and the selector at 0x101645d5 or 0x101645de. ELGACT1 rows at the three instrumented return sites preserve the same base, weapon-output and selector-input order.
findings.consequence: The ordinary player resolver has a pinned order; paired-action ordering is separately recovered, and the player RTTI surface contains no form-specific override order.

findings.fact: CBaseCombatCharacter::Weapon_TranslateActivity delegates to the active weapon's virtual +0x5a4 unless the weapon is absent or excluded.
findings.evidence: 0x10327ec0 resolves the EHANDLE at this+0x19a4, checks the weapon flags, and replaces the incoming activity with the virtual return.
findings.consequence: Weapon-specific locomotion, aim, attack and reload activities come from the weapon class rather than from player-model label matching.

findings.fact: A weapon activity override row is three dwords: base activity, weapon activity and required, exposed by weapon virtuals +0x5a8 and +0x5ac.
findings.evidence: 0x1024edc0 obtains the table pointer/count through those slots, walks at a 12-byte stride and prints Base Act, Weapon Act and Required using the activity-name lookup.
findings.consequence: Every weapon translation table is statically extractable and retail activitydump is an independent oracle for the normalized export.

findings.fact: The pinned binary contains 169 CBaseCombatWeapon subclasses, 61 non-empty per-class activity tables, 58 distinct table blobs and 9,214 ordered per-class rows; CBaseCombatWeapon::ActivityOverride never reads the stored required dword.
findings.evidence: weapon_activity_survey.py validates the binary hash, parses PE32 RTTI, follows vtable +0x5a8/+0x5ac thunks, decodes every 12-byte row and resolves every activity through the 4,460-entry registry. At 0x1024f210, the server walks matching rows in ordinal order, passes each output through owner +0x5e0, accepts it when the body or alternate model has a sequence, and continues to later duplicate-base rows on absence; assembly reads only row offsets 0 and 4 before advancing by 12. The map join resolves 269 of 270 equipment references, with only absent retail classname item_w_sw_m64 unresolved.
findings.consequence: Weapon translation is a closed generated surface. Preserve row order and duplicate-base fallbacks; export required as inert authored provenance, and keep item_w_sw_m64 as an explicit content miss rather than guessing another table.

findings.fact: CBasePlayer::NPC_TranslateActivity maps ACT_WALK_RELAXED to ACT_WALK and ACT_RUN_RELAXED to ACT_RUN and otherwise returns the input unchanged.
findings.evidence: 0x101647a0 compares the input with 0x16 and 0x17 and returns 9 or 0x13 respectively.
findings.consequence: The player applies at least one class-specific translation after a base activity is selected.

findings.fact: CAI_BaseNPC::TranslateActivity applies VtMB's common NPC pre-translation, weapon, class/NPC and availability-fallback order.
findings.evidence: 0x10271ff0 calls virtual +0x5dc on the raw request, virtual +0x5f4 for the first weapon answer, then alternates virtual +0x5e0 and +0x5f4 for at most five iterations. It returns ACT_SCRIPT_CUSTOM_MOVE directly; otherwise it probes the final weapon, remembered class/NPC, first weapon and original candidates with SelectHeaviestSequence and changes an unavailable original ACT_RUN to ACT_WALK.
findings.consequence: The common NPC translation order is closed; the RTTI/vtable survey supplies the complete semantic identity and inheritance of +0x5dc/+0x5e0.

findings.fact: All 77 CAI_BaseNPC descendants collapse to 10 pre-translation bodies, five class-translation bodies and two implementations each of the cover/reload delegates.
findings.evidence: npc_translation_survey.py validates the pinned hash, walks PE32 RTTI, follows vtable +0x5dc/+0x5e0/+0x8e4/+0x8e8 thunks and joins direct plus npc_maker NPCTypE demands. The 22-map corpus has 426 class demands: 425 resolve to exact implementations and only sm_junkyard_1's absent npc_BaseVampAI classname does not.
findings.consequence: Per-class NPC activity translation is a closed generated policy surface; inheritance is retained instead of duplicating 77 switch tables, and the missing Night Watchman class remains explicit.

findings.fact: NPC_EarlyTranslateActivity recognizes 29 paired-action base activities and TranslateBaseGrappleActivity expands each to one of eight contiguous attacker/victim, short/tall and front/back variants.
findings.evidence: 0x104126a0 tests membership in the specially registered base list. 0x10328380 returns base+1, plus one for a tall linked actor, plus two for victim role and plus four for back position; invalid linked state preserves the base. The registry contains all 232 variant names for finishing moves, payphone, feeding, seductive feeding, zombie feeding, sneak attacks and rat feeding.
findings.consequence: Paired actions resolve by an exact arithmetic activity family, not label guessing; the generated catalog must preserve the base plus its eight named roles.

findings.fact: CBasePlayer's paired-action router has nine modes with exact initial activities and six stateful continuation leaves.
findings.evidence: player_grapple_survey.py validates the hash, decodes 0x10328c80 and verifies all five direct StartGrappleAttack calls. Modes 0/1 map to ACT_FEEDING_ENGAGE, 2 to ACT_SEDUCTIVE_ENGAGE, 3/4 to ACT_SNEAKATTACK_SUCCESS/FAILURE, 5 to ACT_PAYPHONE_PICKUP, 6 to ACT_RAT_FEED_ENGAGE, 7 to ACT_FINISHING_MOVE and 8 to ACT_ZOMBIE_FEEDING_ENGAGE. 0x10164240 routes attacker modes 0/1/2/3/5/6/8 through vtable +0x68c/+0x690/+0x694/+0x688/+0x698/+0x69c and uses sequence completion for 4/7; a victim does not drive the pair. Producers supply modes 0/6, 2, 3, 5 and 8, leaving 1/4/7 without a pinned-binary caller.
findings.consequence: Paired player action-to-activity selection is closed, including dormant registered modes; shipped reachability is retained separately from the static mode vocabulary.

findings.fact: Player paired actions use a two-actor activity resolver and commit rather than direct sequence-label playback.
findings.evidence: 0x10328df0 selects the initial base, alignment and role state and enters both actors through virtual +0x5ec. 0x1032a100 resolves the base independently through 0x10328380, weapon-translates each role-specific activity, selects weighted sequences and commits current/ideal state on both; a missing sequence warns and calls 0x10329560 EndGrapple.
findings.consequence: A remake must resolve and commit attacker and victim as one transaction and preserve a hard failure, not guess labels or let each actor advance independently.

findings.fact: The router's first-priority branch protects activity-owned player animation, and contextual compact code 12 owns the vomit state machine while its latch is active.
findings.evidence: 0x10164240 calls vtable +0x670 before testing grapple state. 0x10161200 protects timed ACT_BLOCK/ACT_BLOCK_HEAVY and blocked reactions, unfinished ACT_MELEE_ATTACK through ACT_MELEE_ATTACK_HEAVY, ACT_FEEDING_ENGAGE_FAILURE, knockback/protected ranges 0x75-0x93 plus 0x9d0, and ACT_VOMIT_INTO/IDLE/GETOUT. 0x101641d0 handles code 12 with the +0x1cb0 latch and advances ACT_VOMIT_INTO to IDLE, GETOUT and ACT_IDLE while consuming blood and finally clearing the latch.
findings.consequence: Protected activity ownership is a higher-priority policy than ordinary or paired selection; code 12 cannot be assigned one global activity without its latch/mode context.

findings.fact: The protected melee special-owner branch is inventory handoff, not another animation route.
findings.evidence: When the +0x1df4 gate, protected range, elapsed cycle and active-weapon capability agree, 0x10164240 clears the flag and calls player virtual +0x720 at 0x10170b50. It forwards the owner's classname and +0x4a0 identity to virtual +0x724 at 0x100b7fe0, which searches all 224 inventory slots for that item and may activate/equip it; neither body chooses an activity, sequence or layer.
findings.consequence: The complete protected-router surface has no hidden exact-label or layer producer.

findings.fact: CAI_BaseNPC::ResolveActivityToSequence selects ordinary NPC sequences, exact scripted custom moves, disposition fallbacks and the final sequence-zero fallback.
findings.evidence: 0x10272130 calls TranslateActivity, then SelectWeightedSequence for ordinary requests. A missing translated ACT_RUN retries ACT_WALK; any remaining miss retries ACT_DISPOSITION, delegating through the disposition owner at this+0x98 / virtual +0x98c when present, and a missing disposition becomes sequence 0. ACT_SCRIPT_CUSTOM_MOVE resolves the owner label at this+0x5d74 through LookupSequence and a miss joins the ACT_WALK/disposition tail.
findings.consequence: Ordinary activity selection and exceptional custom-move/disposition fallbacks are explicit resolver routes rather than clip-label heuristics.

findings.fact: NPC ideal activity, immediate activity and transition traversal are separate commit policies.
findings.evidence: 0x10272650 stores and resolves the ideal without committing it; 0x102727d0 re-resolves a changed target and calls 0x102726a0 to traverse transition sequences; 0x102725d0 resolves and calls 0x10272490 immediately. The latter commits the exact sequence and weapon activity while preserving the un-translated logical activity.
findings.consequence: A remake action record must keep requested logical activity, translated activity, weapon activity, target sequence and transition state as separate fields.

findings.fact: The controlled sm_hub_1 corpus contains 1,232 complete common NPC translation resolutions.
findings.evidence: Caller-delimited ELGACT1 paths contain 1,232 first-weapon and heaviest-availability stages across 50 entity indices: 795 continue to the ordinary weighted selector and 437 are resolution-only queries. Grouping by the full serial-bearing entity handle leaves zero incomplete chains and joins ten NPC body lifetimes without index-reuse contamination.
findings.consequence: The captured NPC evidence is a staged resolution map with exact clip-table joins, not a flat sequence histogram.

findings.fact: The first controlled sm_hub_1 corpus joins compact codes 0, 1 and 2 through ordinary player translation to exact sequence identities on tremere_Male_Armor_0.
findings.evidence: The hash-gated ELGACT1 database contains 72,440 records (6,197 PCLS, 6,077 IDEA, 26,757 WTRN, 4,214 SWGT and 29,195 SHVY), marks all four operator beats and passes every verifier gate. The clip-table join resolves walk=5, run=4, sneak=7, crouch=8, leap=1407, falling=1410 and land=1411 with exact owner banks. Crouch is selected three times and reused for 151 requests; its longest uninterrupted run is 54 classifier samples / 1.791 seconds.
findings.consequence: The three-Cs locomotion slice and pre-completion held-request reuse are trace-backed independently of the static completion/restart proof.

findings.fact: A sustained unarmed crouch repeats the same non-looping sequence after it finishes.
findings.evidence: CBaseAnimating::StudioFrameAdvance at 0x1008f120 clamps a completed non-looping sequence and sets m_bSequenceFinished at +0x65c. In 0x101644f0, that flag makes an unchanged activity dirty at 0x10164595 and forces ResetSequenceInfo even when weighted selection returns the unchanged sequence at 0x101645f1. ResetSequenceInfo at 0x10090950 clears both the finished flag and cycle. ACT_CROUCH has only sequence 8 on the validated player body.
findings.consequence: The faithful player graph must reuse crouch before completion and restart sequence 8 on completion; holding its terminal frame is a divergence.

findings.fact: The controlled ordinary jump selects ACT_LEAP, then ACT_FALLING, then a moving gait or ACT_LAND; it does not select ACT_LEAP_ASCEND or ACT_LEAP_DESCEND.
findings.evidence: Compact code 2 is observed with jump/landing state 1 selecting sequence 1407, state 7 selecting sequence 1410, and state 8 selecting translated ACT_WALK sequence 5 while moving or ACT_LAND sequence 1411 while still. The one ducked state-8 ACT_LAND_CROUCH request returns -1.
findings.consequence: The player graph uses leap/falling/land states and gives ACT_LAND_CROUCH a named missing-sequence fallback instead of treating the authored ascend/descend clips as observed gameplay.

findings.fact: The server-side block animation endpoint is compact code 13 to ACT_PREBLOCK.
findings.evidence: input_action_survey.py proves +wpn_secondaryatk presses a dedicated client kbutton packed as held bit 0x08000000 and then forwards into +attack2. Server 0x10160ec0 tests that exact bit with ground and weapon-capability gates; 0x1016bb50 returns 13 on success, and 0x10164870 maps code 13 to registered activity 0x1154 ACT_PREBLOCK.
findings.consequence: The block producer is closed end to end: +attack2 alone is not the block verb, while held +wpn_secondaryatk reaches PLAYER_BLOCK then ACT_PREBLOCK.

findings.fact: The 22-map exported corpus contains 198 live exact-label map requests and 18 SetAnimation wires, each with an explicit owner-model disposition.
findings.evidence: action_animation_survey.py joins 134 scripted-sequence labels, 64 LoopSequence labels and 18 SetAnimation parameters to npc_manifest v6. Of the 198 map labels, 184 resolve through the manifest, three are verified single-frame static models intentionally omitted from it, and eleven are authored label misses. All 18 SetAnimation wires resolve.
findings.consequence: The current map corpus's authored exact-sequence producer surface is closed; remaining producer RE is native task/class/layer logic or belongs to maps outside the current export.

findings.fact: A missing scripted_sequence or aiscripted_sequence exact label warns and plays sequence zero rather than entering the activity resolver.
findings.evidence: 0x101a82d0 and 0x101a9510 call LookupSequence, test for -1, emit their unknown scripted-sequence warning, write sequence 0, zero the cycle and call ResetSequenceInfo. The current misses are ACT_COWER on three diner actors, pre_fight_bow on AsianVamp and ACT_DOORKNOCK on the player controller.
findings.consequence: ACT_* text authored in m_iszPlay is still an exact-label request; the remake must preserve the sequence-zero miss route.

findings.fact: Character.SetGesture is an exact-label route whose missing-label behavior is a silent no-op.
findings.evidence: 0x10197f60 calls LookupSequence on the character component at entity+0x98 and only starts the gesture when the result is non-negative. Both shipped calls, Tourette's malk_female_idle and SM_Huddle, are absent from her complete include-model vocabulary.
findings.consequence: The two shipped SetGesture calls animate nothing and must not be mapped to guessed activities or sequence zero.

findings.fact: The pinned binary registers 330 contiguous common/Troika task IDs and compiles 691 schedules containing 4,139 task invocations.
findings.evidence: 0x10316ff0 registers TASK_INVALID=0 through TASK_PLAY_DEATH_SEQUENCE=0x149. native_schedule_survey.py decodes the compiled schedule constructors and finds 441 distinct task names, including 378 explicit activity arguments covering 84 ACT_* values.
findings.consequence: Schedule demand is reproducible ordered data; a task name alone is not an animation route until its StartTask/RunTask handler is classified.

findings.fact: CAI_BaseNPC and CAI_BaseNPCTroika schedule tasks request activities rather than exact labels, including the misleading TASK_PLAY_SEQUENCE family.
findings.evidence: 0x102827f0 and 0x102a1910 pass TASK_SET_ACTIVITY, TASK_PLAY_SEQUENCE, TASK_PLAY_SEQUENCE_PRIVATE, TASK_PLAY_SEQUENCE_FACE_ENEMY and TASK_PLAY_SEQUENCE_FACE_TARGET arguments to SetIdealActivity. Attack/reload/special tasks choose their fixed ACT_* values; TASK_PLAY_DEATH_SEQUENCE tries its argument, ACT_DIESIMPLE, then ACT_IDLE.
findings.consequence: Compiled schedule arguments must enter the common activity translator/resolver; they must never be looked up as sequence names.

findings.fact: VtMB's Troika tasks expose three distinct animation commit policies: ideal-activity playback, immediate loop/blend activity playback, and a timed activity-owned gesture layer.
findings.evidence: 0x102a1910 uses SetIdealActivity for ordinary activity tasks, ResolveActivityToSequence plus SetActivity for TASK_DO_LOOP_ACTIVITY and the blend variants, and SelectWeightedSequence plus the four-slot overlay API for TASK_ADD_GESTURE. 0x102aacf0 reasserts loop/blend activities until their completion condition.
findings.consequence: The task-to-animation map must retain base-sequence versus overlay ownership and StartTask versus RunTask continuation separately.

findings.fact: The complete NPC task-override surface contains 330 shared and 184 class-local task registrations, 29 distinct StartTask bodies, 24 distinct RunTask bodies and 49 custom handler bodies across all 77 CAI_BaseNPC descendants.
findings.evidence: npc_task_override_survey.py validates the pinned hash, walks RTTI vtable slots +0x6e8/+0x6f0, decodes 20 class-local registration owners and materializes 100 policy rows covering 111 task routes. Thirty-one custom bodies add direct animation policy and 18 add none; bounded direct-call analysis finds zero custom exact-label and zero custom layer routes.
findings.consequence: The schedule/task action map is closed for current and out-of-corpus boss/monster classes. Every custom animation branch enters activity resolution; exact-label and overlay behavior remain only in their separately identified common/script routes.

findings.fact: Eighteen custom NPC task bodies introduce no direct animation request before delegation.
findings.evidence: The full task-slot survey classifies AsianVampire, Cop, SabbatGunman, SheriffMan and base VampireBoss custom starts plus the non-animation custom runs separately from the 31 animation-bearing bodies. AsianVampire setup chooses jump geometry, Scurrying evade tasks update bookkeeping, and base VampireBoss transformation creates/hands off the MorphModel NPC; its schedule requests ACT_IDLE through the common TASK_SET_ACTIVITY route.
findings.consequence: State, navigation, spawning, damage and timing work remains distinct from action selection, and no exact-label request may be inferred from a custom task merely because its schedule leads to animation elsewhere.

findings.fact: The current exported producer corpus carries three MorphModel fields, no SetModel or Transform I/O wires, and 356 executable Python SetModel calls.
findings.evidence: action_animation_survey.py records 161 literal model-selection paths and 198 dynamic expressions across map/Python producers. Fifty-four literals select owners present in npc_manifest v6; 107 select static, weapon, viewmodel or other models outside the character-animation manifest.
findings.consequence: Model selection is an owner-bank change, not a clip request; later activity/label resolution must use the selected model while non-character selections remain explicitly outside the character manifest.

findings.fact: The player_sequence console command bypasses activity translation and resolves an exact sequence label.
findings.evidence: 0x10348560 reads the command argument, calls LookupSequence at 0x1008f7b0, writes this+0x6f0, calls ResetSequenceInfo at 0x10090950 and zeros the cycle.
findings.consequence: Direct authored/developer sequence requests require a separate resolver route from ordinary gameplay activities.

findings.fact: The v2531 StudioSeqDesc event record is 76 bytes: float cycle, signed event ID, signed type and a fixed 64-byte options string, addressed descriptor-relative by numevents/eventindex at +20/+24.
findings.evidence: animation_event_survey.py validates all 4,445 patch-first MDLs and finds 1,150 event-bearing sequences, 1,872 events, 58 event IDs, 82 options strings, type zero on every record, no invalid cycle or record and a maximum of 11 events on one sequence.
findings.consequence: Sequence events are closed model metadata and can be exported directly; their record must not be replaced by a modern Source event struct.

findings.fact: Server DispatchAnimEvents scans 76-byte records, dispatches only event IDs below 5000 over the half-open cycle interval, handles looping wrap once and calls OnSequenceFinish when the sequence newly completes.
findings.evidence: 0x10091880 preserves the last checked cycle at animating+0x658, copies cycle, ID, the complete options field and source pointer into the runtime event, calls virtual +0x40c, and visits the wrapped interval after a loop crosses 1.0.
findings.consequence: Event timing and the server/client 5000 boundary are exact playback policy, not an exporter convention.

findings.fact: The complete native sequence-event surface is finite: 300 server animating classes use 20 HandleAnimEvent bodies, 169 server weapon classes use seven Operator_HandleAnimEvent bodies, 237 client animating classes use three FireEvent bodies and all 214 client weapons share one viewmodel event hook.
findings.evidence: animation_event_survey.py hash-pins vampire.dll and client.dll, walks MSVC RTTI and validates every effective body against its decompiled policy ledger. Server events include scripted, footstep, weapon, attachment, sound and model actions; client events include muzzle flashes, sounds, bodygroups, ACT_* sequence changes and attachment/origin effects.
findings.consequence: Native event dispatch RE is closed. ANM4b must now emit the decoded timeline and implement the documented handlers; no per-class event behavior may be guessed from model options alone.

findings.fact: Every model-declared autolayer is evaluated at its host cycle and accumulated at literal caller weight 1.0 in authored entry order.
findings.evidence: animation_layer_survey.py validates 4,445 MDLs / 14,012 sequences, rejects the seven known malformed count-764 tails and resolves 461 hosts / 685 entries with zero self-reference, recursion, out-of-range target or target activity. In pinned client.dll, 0x1008a0ce pushes 0x3f800000 as FUN_10088e10 parameter 7 after recursive FUN_10089c40 evaluation.
findings.consequence: The model autolayer scalar and order are closed: ordinary layers blend and delta layers accumulate at full caller weight times each target animation's per-bone mask.

findings.fact: Base-sequence transitions and the separate four-slot combat layer stack have complete composition and interruption order.
findings.evidence: Client transition records append without a cap, fade independently with SimpleSpline and compose newest previous to oldest unless the incoming sequence requests a hard cut. Server SetLayer at 0x10099020 initializes weight 0.1, cycle 0, playback rate 1 and two inert 0.2 blend fields; base pose then active slots compose in ascending index order, and replacement/removal kills a slot immediately.
findings.consequence: Layer/override/interruption order is no longer an RE37 question. Export/bake and graph implementation must preserve these three distinct stages rather than merge model autolayers, base crossfades and networked combat slots.

findings.fact: The installed player-body union resolves 56 target models through 122 owner models to 3,330 exact sequence descriptors and 3,615 animation descriptors with no missing includes.
findings.evidence: research/tooling/capture/inventory_player_animations.py generated the hash-closed cap12 inventory from clandoc000.txt and the patch-first model tree; the sequences contain 1,202 distinct non-empty activity literals.
findings.consequence: Coverage is keyed by exact owner model and raw sequence index, not by label, and is generated rather than maintained by hand.

functions.label: base_animating_dispatch_anim_events
functions.role: CBaseAnimating::DispatchAnimEvents; scans 76-byte sequence events below ID 5000 over the current and looping-wrap cycle intervals, calls HandleAnimEvent +0x40c, then OnSequenceFinish.

functions.label: base_animating_handle_anim_event
functions.role: Base server HandleAnimEvent body for named-attachment state events 2070/2071 and options-named weighted sequence event 4005.

functions.label: npc_handle_anim_event
functions.role: CAI_BaseNPC HandleAnimEvent; owns scripted, movement-yaw, item/weapon and footstep families before combat-character fallback.

functions.label: npc_troika_handle_anim_event
functions.role: CAI_BaseNPCTroika HandleAnimEvent; adds facial/breath, timed activity layer and Troika attachment/movement/interesting-place event families.

functions.label: combat_character_handle_anim_event
functions.role: CBaseCombatCharacter HandleAnimEvent; forwards every weapon-range or foreign-source event to active-weapon Operator_HandleAnimEvent +0x5c8 and owns weapon state, sound and attached-model events.

functions.label: ranged_weapon_operator_handle_anim_event
functions.role: Shared ranged-weapon +0x5c8 handler; routes 3030..3044 through the fire-state transition and 4001/4002 through bodygroup state.

functions.label: base_weapon_operator_handle_anim_event
functions.role: Base combat-weapon +0x5c8 warning body used by 17 weapon classes and as the unhandled fallback for ranged/melee/inventory policies.

functions.label: tzimisce_melee_operator_handle_anim_event
functions.role: Tzimisce melee +0x5c8 handler; swallows 3003 and maps 3045/3046 to its two gated attack variants before common-melee fallback.

functions.label: common_melee_operator_handle_anim_event
functions.role: Shared common-melee +0x5c8 handler for 29 classes; accepts the melee/ranged compatibility no-op set, gated event 3047 and bodygroup events 4001/4002.

functions.label: ming_melee_operator_handle_anim_event
